stem:
Just after sunset, Bilal sees a thin bright crescent low in the western sky, near where the Sun went down. Most of the Moon's disc looks dark.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: The Moon is roughly toward the Sun as seen from Earth, so little of its illuminated half faces Earth.
This thin crescent is consistent with a phase near new Moon, not with a full Moon.
The Moon must be nearly opposite the Sun because any bright part means a full Moon.
The illuminated portion facing Earth changes only after the observed phase has already changed.

teacher.key_rationale: A thin crescent near the Sun's direction means the Moon is toward the Sun and little of the lit half faces Earth. Full Moon needs the Moon nearly opposite the Sun. Geometry of illumination sets the phase, not the other way around.
